newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares hit new records as chemicals surge.
newsitem.headline: German shares hit new records as chemicals surge.

text.p: German shares hit record heights on Wednesday, with the 30-share DAX led higher by an upsurge in chemical shares to hurdle the psychologically key 3,100 point level in post-bourse trade.

The IBIS DAX index ended the day up 47.25 points, or 1.5 percent, at 3,114.73, amid gains of some four percent on shares in chemical giants Hoechst and Bayer, which had lagged firmly behind the broader market's recent rally.
Earlier the DAX ended bourse trade up one percent at 3,098.00 points, just shy of the key 3,100 level.

The advance were underpinned by a firm dollar, seen as a strong plus for German exporters, early gains on Wall Street and growing confidence that interest rates are set to remain steady for the time being.

Other market stars included airline Deutsche Lufthansa, rallying after announcing a restructure that would drastically streamline its management structure to end the day up five percent at 23.35 marks.

But the chemical sector showed a consistently strong performance, generally rising at least twice as fast as the market average. Bayer ended up 2.72 marks at 64.80 and Hoechst closed at 72.05 marks, up 2.70 marks.
Top chemical shares are still trading well below highs hit in early December, since which the DAX has risen eight percent.
"It had to happen some time," said a trader at a major foreign bank in Frankfurt. "We have had chemicals on our buy list since last week -- it didn't make sense that they all peaked last year."
Dealers said more gains were on the cards for the chemicals sector although immediate prospects for the broader share market, having breached another key resistance level, were less clear.

News due at 1915 GMT of the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee's meeting on interest rates and tomorrow's regular Bundesbank council policy meeting will be key, but the consensus in Germany was that no rate changes are coming.
